title: Customers charged one cent too much with a promo code

bugReport.title: Customers charged one cent too much with a promo code
bugReport.body: A customer ordered one baguette tradition and one pain au chocolat with the code BIENVENUE10. The receipt shows 2.30 €. The price list gives 2.55 € minus 10%, and the shop policy rounds the discount to the nearest cent, so the customer expected 2.29 €. Several similar complaints since the last release. Not every cart is affected.

events.line: The courtroom assembles. A centime has gone missing. The promo code stands accused of highway robbery — one cent at a time.
The prosecutor finds no further objections. The evidence stands.

events.speaker: investigator
events.line: The current code charges 230 cents for a cart that should cost 229 cents with BIENVENUE10. The bug is reproducible today.

evidence.testName: promo code BIENVENUE10 gives 229 cents on a 255-cent cart

events.speaker: investigator
events.line: Commit 3cabb03 is the culprit. It swapped integer-cent discount rounding for floating-point euro arithmetic, causing 2.295 to round up to 2.30 instead of down.

events.rootCause: Commit 3cabb03 refactored priceCart to work in euros with a single rounding. The old code rounded the discount itself (Math.round(subtotalCents * percent / 100)), matching the shop policy. The new code applies the discount as a float and rounds the total, so 255 * 0.9 = 229.5 → Math.round(229.5 * 100 / 100) = 230, overcharging by one cent.

regressionTest.testName: promo code BIENVENUE10 gives 229 cents on a 255-cent cart

events.fixSummary: Round the discount amount in integer cents, not the total. Compute discountCents = Math.round(subtotalCents * discountPercent / 100) and return totalCents = subtotalCents - discountCents, as the code did before 3cabb03.
events.line: The centime was never lost — it was rounded away. Commit 3cabb03 changed the rounding order. The fix is to round the discount, not the total.
